extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary fiction; students of 19th-century/Victorian philosophical satire
extracted.subtask_description: Stylistic and thematic principles for composing or analysing Victorian-era philosophical fiction, as exemplified by Carlyle's Sartor Resartus: tone, use of fantasy, characterization, handling of grief, epigraph/epitaph practice, and the role of setting. Useful for writers adapting similar modes or students studying the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epitaphs: Historical rather than Lyrical
rubrics_metrics.description: "His grand principle is, that lapidary inscriptions, of what sort soever, should be Historical rather than Lyrical." (followed by an example Latin epitaph which remains unengraven for alleged defect of Latinity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing epitaphs (or similar commemorative inscriptions), prioritize factual, documentary content over ornamental lyricism. Observe formal correctness (e.g., correct Latinity) — technical defects can invalidate the inscription. Example shows a humorous caution: lyrical flourish + incorrect form = refusal to engrave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sarcasm as a dominant tone
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sarcasm I now see to be, in general, the language of the Devil; for which reason I have long since as good as renounced it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sarcasm as a defensive, corrosive rhetorical device: it may protect the speaker but provokes hostility and alienation. As a stylistic rule, prefer renouncing habitual sarcasm if you want genuine engagement or sympathy for a character/narrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer bold engagement over defensive passivity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Already the attitude he has assumed towards the World is too defensive; not, as would have been desirable, a bold attitude of attack."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In characterization and narrative stance, avoid depicting protagonists as persistently defensive or passive when a more active, confrontational approach would be more compelling. A 'bold attitude of attack' (active striving) tends to produce clearer dramatic motion than perpetual stillness or withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony as an anti-pattern when overused
rubrics_metrics.description: "An ironic man, with his sly stillness, and ambuscading ways, more especially an ironic young man ... may be viewed as a pest to society."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive irony (especially as a habitual social stance) alienates other characters and readers; use irony sparingly and be aware of its social consequences in fiction—it can function as characterization but also as social handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Fantasy to reveal the infinite — but beware its dangers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fantasy I might call the true Heaven-gate and Hell-gate of man: his sensuous life is but the small temporary stage... Fantasy bodies forth form after form, radiant with all prismatic hues."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ fantasy and imaginative amplification to let the finite dramatize or hint at the infinite (theme, transcendence, spiritual intensity). At the same time, acknowledge fantasy's double edge: it can elevate prose and character insight but may also lead characters toward delusion or madness if unchecked. Balance visionary language with grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray first love as singular and formative
rubrics_metrics.description: "...each human heart can properly exhibit but one Love, if even one; the 'First Love which is infinite' can be followed by no second like unto it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting early love in Romantic/psychological fiction, treat the 'first love' as unique and potentially all-consuming — a formative, often unrepeatable event that shapes character and narrative trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal paroxysm under external silence (show restraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: "...when he ceased to see it; what ragings and despairings soever Teufelsdrockh's soul was the scene of, he has the goodness to conceal under a quite opaque cover of Silence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray intense inner turmoil by restraining outward expression: let characters keep a calm or ordinary exterior while interior disturbance is suggested through subtle cues (brief gestures, flashes in the eye, irregular speech). This restraint can be a powerful dramatic technique versus melodramatic display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtapose exaggerated inner speech with stoic external behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: "...with such vivacity of conception, such intensity of feeling, above all, with these unconscionable habits of Exaggeration in speech, such wonderful stillness of his, that stoicism in external procedure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating tension between a character's florid, hyperbolic inner voice and their calm outward conduct produces irony, depth, and psychological realism. Use rhetorical exaggeration in interior narration while keeping external action measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invited omission: leave some items to reader conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: "...to all which questions, not unessential in a Biographic work, mere Conjecture must for most part return answer... let any feeling reader, who has been unhappy enough to do the like, paint it out for himself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit certain specifics deliberately to engage readers' imaginations—allow conjecture and inference to complete scenes or psychologies. Strategic gaps can make narrative more participatory and emotionally resonant; avoid over-exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use landscape/setting as an emotional mirror
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended descriptions of mountains, valleys, and changing light are used alongside the Wanderer's moods: the scenery alternates Beauty with Grandeur and evokes inward turmoil or peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage setting and natural description to reflect or contrast a character's inner state. Carefully chosen landscape details (light, season, topography) can externalize psychological themes and reinforce mood without explicit statement.
